title: fix: attribute sign-ins to the real URL, not the TanStack route id
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- `page_viewed` reported TanStack's `routeId` (`/_dashboard/news`); `sign_in_started`'s server-side `referringSource()` reads the real `Referer` URL (`/news`, since `/_dashboard` is a pathless layout with no URL segment). The two never matched, so every sign-in start made from a dashboard page (News, Models, Pollen, Keys, etc.) was silently dropped from attribution — 199 of 280 starts from our own origin since the split went live.
- This also invalidated an earlier read of the dashboard: content-page → sign-in looked like 0% conversion, which drove a wrong recommendation to add a sign-in CTA. The button already exists on every dashboard page; the 0% was a measurement artifact, not missing UI.
- Fix: report `location.pathname` instead of `routeId`, and shrink the page enum to real URL paths (`/news` not `/_dashboard/news`). No mapping table — one vocabulary instead of two.
- Updates the one hardcoded page string in `kpi_signup_funnel.pipe` and the test fixture to match.

gist.headline: The routes found their way home
gist.blurb: Dashboard sign-ins were taking a scenic detour through TanStack’s internal route IDs. Analytics now follows the real URL trail, so the funnel can count the bees that were there all along.
gist.summary: Fixed dashboard sign-in attribution by reporting location.pathname (such as /news) instead of TanStack routeId values (such as /_dashboard/news), aligning page_viewed events with referringSource() and the signup-funnel KPI.
gist.impact: Dashboard-origin sign-in starts from News, Models, Pollen, Keys, and other real URL paths now match their page views instead of being silently excluded from attribution.

A tiny CRT monitor robot compares matching page-view and sign-in trail markers, representing the restored funnel attribution.
